item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the required Upload API, validates inputs, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves Add unchanged, and routes through Add. A changes Add’s behavior and bypasses it from Upload, violating two explicit architectural requirements.","reasons":["B preserves FilesService.Add and calls it from Upload, retaining existing option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.","B explicitly validates both an empty filename and nil content before constructing a request.","B uses the established multipartbody.NewFile helper with the required field name \"file\" and exact API signature.","A makes every Add call eagerly read and buffer the supplied body, changing the lower-level API’s streaming and error-timing behavior despite the requirement to preserve it unchanged and limit buffering to Upload’s encoded body path when appropriate. It also routes Upload through a new private add method instead of FilesService.Add itself."],"risks_a":["The new io.ReadAll in Add can increase memory use for custom multipart bodies and changes when reader failures occur.","Upload has no visible explicit filename/content validation and has no validation or source-reader-error tests.","The new private add method duplicates the role the contract assigns to the existing Add method."],"risks_b":["It unnecessarily adds PersonsService.UploadPicture and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the requested convenience API.","The Upload multipart test checks the field and filename but never asserts uploaded content.","The retry test counts requests but does not inspect the body on both attempts, so it does not directly prove streamed content was replayed unchanged; validation and source-reader-error tests are also missing."]}
